artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega,F=(J,H))$ be a semitoric integrable system on a connected $4$-dimensional symplectic manifold; that is, $J$ and $H$ are smooth functions in involution, the momentum map $F:M\to\mathbb{R}^2$ is proper, $J$ generates an effective Hamiltonian $S^1$-action, and all singularities of $F$ are non-degenerate with no hyperbolic components. Assume $F$ has a focus-focus critical point $m\in M$ with critical value $c=F(m)\in\mathbb{R}^2$. Associated with such a focus-focus point is the Taylor series symplectic invariant: a formal power series $S^\infty\in\mathbb{R}[[X,Y]]$ (with $S^\infty(0,0)=0$ and $S^\infty$ defined modulo $2\pi X$) which is the semi-global symplectic invariant of the singular Lagrangian fibration of $F$ in a neighborhood of the focus-focus fiber $F^{-1}(c)$.

Consider a semiclassical quantization of the system by a pair of commuting self-adjoint (pseudodifferential or Berezin-Toeplitz) operators $\hat J(\hbar),\hat H(\hbar)$ whose principal symbols are $J,H$, and denote by
$$\Sigma(\hbar)=\operatorname{JointSpec}(\hat J(\hbar),\hat H(\hbar))\subset\mathbb{R}^2$$
their joint spectrum.

Problem. Give an explicit algorithm that recovers the Taylor series invariant $S^\infty$ associated with the focus-focus critical value $c$ directly from the asymptotic behaviour, as $\hbar\to 0^+$, of the part of the joint spectrum $\Sigma(\hbar)$ lying in an arbitrarily small neighborhood of $c$, using a singular Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization rule at the focus-focus singularity.
artifact.category_tag: semitoric integrable systems and inverse spectral theory
artifact.status_search_result: Le Floch and Pelayo (2021, "The inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems", arXiv:2104.06704) provide explicit formulas recovering all symplectic invariants—including the Taylor series invariant at each focus-focus singularity—from the semiclassical asymptotics of the joint spectrum of pseudodifferential or Berezin-Toeplitz quantizations, using singular Bohr-Sommerfeld rules. Earlier work in the Jaynes-Cummings setting (Le Floch, Pelayo, Vũ Ngọc) had already established the focus-focus case in that example.

status_evidence.title: The inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit formulas recover, from the semiclassical asymptotics of the joint spectrum, all symplectic invariants of the underlying classical semitoric system.
status_evidence.claim: The Taylor series invariant of a semitoric system is recovered from the joint spectrum near focus-focus values.

status_evidence.title: Inverse spectral theory for semiclassical Jaynes-Cummings systems
status_evidence.snippet: The Taylor series and the Eliasson diffeomorphism are invariants of a singular Lagrangian fibration near a focus-focus fiber; techniques compute them explicitly from the joint spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: The Taylor series invariant can be computed from spectral data using singular Bohr-Sommerfeld rules.

status_evidence.title: One can hear semitoric systems — San Vu Ngoc
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum semitoric systems can be reconstructed from their joint spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Reconstruction of semitoric invariants from joint spectrum is established.
